do.rule: Whenever instructional cleaning or preparation steps are spoken (emptying, rinsing, drying), show the specific action or prop rather than a character standing passively.
Ensure captions maintain adequate spacing from the top edge in all vertical frames.
Ensure key visual props and characters mentioned in the voiceover are rendered in the scene.
Maintain correct side-gripping of the gourd for all characters handling mate to preserve physical realism.
Ensure handheld props attach directly to ball hands without gaps.
Keep upper screen region clear of overlapping character faces during UI overlays.
Maintain the correct side-grasping grip for all characters holding gourds across all frames.
Ensure object scales like yerba packages and thermos flasks remain consistent across all office scenes.
Maintain correct relative sizing between oversized props like the cuia and the characters holding them.
Always keep floating ball hands visibly attached via perspective and actively gripping props.
Maintain clear proportional scaling between thermos and gourds across close-up and wide shots.
Keep floating-hand characters within the inner safe zone to prevent edge cropping on narrow 9:16 vertical viewports.
Align pouring spouts vertically above liquid targets for convincing flow physics.
Keep human characters sized to roughly half the vertical 9:16 frame height in indoor/patio scenes rather than shrinking them to fit oversized background furniture.
When the script specifically mentions an action and prop like dumping into a sink ('pileta'), render the sink and pouring motion rather than placing an abstract red X over a generic pose.

avoid.rule: Never place graphic warning marks, text, or crosses over character faces.
Do not mix flat vector templates into pixel8 reels.
Avoid using generic placeholder geometry when specific object flaws are narrated.
Avoid overlapping multiple caption boxes when several family members are grouped together in a single frame.
Never place headline text boxes directly over raised hands or facial expressions.
Avoid repeating identical static frames across consecutive shots without visual progression.
Do not isolate props onto abstract pedestals when the narrative is about the character carrying them.
Avoid overly plain text lists without contextual illustrations in infographic frames.
Do not repeat identical background asset clusters side by side without varying scale or spacing.
Avoid showing modern mate props (straws/bombillas) during historical origins scenes explaining life before them.
Avoid cropping character foreheads directly beneath multi-line text cards.
Never render handheld props (mate, flasks, cups) without attaching an arm and curling hand explicitly grasping them.
Do not render callout pill badges pointing to a prop when the main headline already states the exact same phrase.
Avoid duplicating large focal props like parrillas or hearths within the same backdrop.
Avoid placing headline text boxes across character eye lines in close-ups.
Avoid placing isolated, shrunken full-body figures in oversized empty rooms.
Avoid T-pose or wide floating hand placements when characters hold no props.
Avoid reusing the exact same static close-up frame multiple times consecutively without a change in expression, angle, or action.
Avoid using board templates that display only plain text without any visual icons, props, or characters.
